subject: Automotive & EVs
title: How a Battery Stores Energy
description: A short lesson to help you apply How a Battery Stores Energy.

hook.text: A battery is a chemical machine—it stores energy by rearranging atoms, not by holding electricity.

buildup.text: Inside, a chemical reaction at one electrode releases electrons that flow to the other electrode.

discovery.text: That electron flow through an external circuit is what we call electric current—usable power.

twist.text: Rechargeable batteries can reverse the reaction, pushing electrons back and restoring the original chemistry.

climax.text: Every EV on the road runs on this simple principle—chemistry converting to motion through electrons.

punchline.text: Batteries don't store electricity—they store chemistry.

quiz.question: How does a battery actually store energy?
options: It holds a charge like a capacitor
